clue.text: Page with original phrase, possibly

indicators.note: read as 'novel, newly made', so the word phrase is reworked into fresh order

explanation.surface: A page carrying a phrase from an original source, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words express uncertainty: something that may or may not be the case.

clue.text: Resolve single error in calculation

explanation.surface: Someone sorting out one slip in their arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase literally: in a sum with one mistake, a single figure is out.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out a problem is to settle it; and one wrong digit means a figure is out, i.e. off.

clue.text: Greek island's streets in sound

indicators.note: the clue asks for the word spoken rather than written, giving a spelling with the same pronunciation

parts.note: streets are roads

explanation.surface: The roads of a Greek island described as being in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'in good repair' describing the streets, but it signals that ROADS is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the Dodecanese, an Aegean isle famed for its ancient Colossus.

clue.text: Evaluate a twopenny increase

parts.note: two pence is 2P, written as two Ps
to increase is to raise

explanation.surface: Weighing up whether a pay rise of two pence is worth anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate something is to assess or value it.

clue.text: This kind of treatment is off-putting

definitions.text: This kind of treatment is off-putting

parts.words: This kind of treatment is off-putting
parts.note: a remedy that works by making a habit repellent is literally designed to put the patient off it

explanation.surface: A complaint that some medical regime is unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychological method pairing an unwanted behaviour with discomfort so the patient comes to dislike it.

clue.text: Favouring one kind of words for religious book

parts.note: pro means in favour of
verbs are one class of words, as are nouns and adjectives

explanation.surface: Preferring a certain vocabulary when writing scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of the Old Testament, collected wise sayings attributed to Solomon.

clue.text: Provide place for a daughter at us university

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is an American university

explanation.surface: Finding a place for one's daughter at an American college.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone in is to give them room or entry.

clue.text: Composing piece of music for particular words

definitions.text: piece of music for particular words

explanation.surface: Writing a musical arrangement for a given text.
explanation.definitionFit: Typesetting is composing type; and a musical arrangement of a poem or text is a version of it.

clue.text: In some quarters, aspiration that's relatively recent

parts.note: N and E are compass points, often called quarters
an aspiration is a wish or hope

explanation.surface: A recently formed hope held in some circles.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish softens the word to 'fairly new', not brand new.

clue.text: It could be minor, yet it's clearly not!

definitions.text: It could be minor, yet it's clearly not!

indicators.note: says the letters of the following words could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that something supposedly small is plainly huge.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a monstrous wrong is anything but minor.
explanation.definitionFit: Great wickedness or vast scale, the opposite of something trivial.

clue.text: Is it advisable for monarch to bear something like this?

parts.note: asking whether one ought to do something is asking 'should?'
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Asking whether the sovereign ought to carry such a burden.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'Should ER bear something like this?': the verb meaning bear is also the body part one carries loads on.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a burden or responsibility, as in carrying it on one's back.

clue.text: Involve in late changes

indicators.note: points to the preceding words being altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting caught up in last-minute alterations.
explanation.definitionFit: To necessitate something as a consequence, to bring it along with it.

clue.text: A crowd joining king and I for sporting party

parts.note: to crowd is to press, and a press is a throng
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A throng joining royalty and the speaker at a sports event party.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'after skiing': the socialising held at a resort once the slopes close.

clue.text: Academic pair love, kiss, and join together

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O
X is the cross for a kiss at the end of a letter
to bridge is to span or connect

explanation.surface: A couple of scholars falling in love, kissing and getting married.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend of Oxford and Cambridge, England's two oldest universities, spoken of as a pair.

clue.text: Original choice crucial in rough sport

indicators.note: original as in creative or inventive, so the word choice is made into something new

parts.note: something crucial is key

explanation.surface: A vital first pick in a physical game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' looks like it means first letter of 'choice', but it rearranges the whole word into ICEHOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast contact game played on a rink with sticks and a puck, known for body checking.

clue.text: Huge sound coming from part of London

indicators.note: the pronunciation of the place name gives a word spelt differently

parts.note: Wapping is a riverside district of East London

explanation.surface: A loud noise heard from a London neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal for enormous, very big.

clue.text: Needlework absorbs a little time, note

indicators.note: one word takes the other into itself, as a sponge absorbs water

parts.note: crochet is needlework done with a hooked needle
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Doing needlework takes up a bit of time, someone observes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like 'take note', but it is the definition: a crotchet is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter note in music, a crotchet lasting one beat in common time.

clue.text: Stagger everyone in tiny island

parts.note: to rock is to sway or stagger
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone reeling on a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: An uninhabited islet in the North Atlantic, famous from the shipping forecast.

clue.text: Calm down if embraced by girl

indicators.note: being held in someone's arms, so the short word sits within the name

parts.note: Molly is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl soothing someone in a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify or appease someone who is angry.

clue.text: Argument with former PM, our equivalent of Charles de Gaulle

definitions.text: our equivalent of Charles de Gaulle

parts.note: Edward Heath was British Prime Minister 1970-74
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A quarrel with an ex-premier, likened to a French president.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles de Gaulle looks like the statesman, but it is the Paris airport; HEATHROW is London's main airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris's main airport is named after de Gaulle; London's chief hub is Britain's counterpart.

clue.text: An Arab craft? Very much so!

parts.note: a dhow is a lateen-sailed Arab boat

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly agreeing that a vessel is Arabian.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic exclamation of agreement, like 'absolutely!'.

clue.text: It's hard covering the ground, as required by vice-captain

indicators.note: the letters needed sit within the hyphenated phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A tough job of covering the pitch, demanded by the deputy skipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering the ground' looks like a fielder's task in cricket, but it describes a layer of ice over land.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent sheet of ice over polar land, a frozen layer on the earth.

clue.text: Having caught fish, hold on tight

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
ling is a long food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler grips hard after landing a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip or hang on firmly.

clue.text: Purge one dreadful clue that could produce this?

definitions.text: Purge one dreadful clue that could produce this?

parts.note: to purge is to rid
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the word clue is mangled, as badly written things are

explanation.surface: Get rid of one awful crossword clue, since it might earn mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a terrible clue would draw scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Mockery or derision, the reaction a really bad clue might provoke.

clue.text: Bishop takes a mineral like quartz into cathedral

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
silica, silicon dioxide, occurs naturally as quartz

explanation.surface: A bishop brings quartz-like stone into his cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A large oblong church with nave and aisles, some of which serve as cathedrals.

clue.text: Just failing to get contract that's unique

explanation.surface: Narrowly missing out on a one-of-a-kind deal.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge, a declarer who makes one trick fewer than bid is said to be one down, or one off.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge contract missed by a single trick; and something made only once, singular.

clue.text: Publicly promote fruit, we hear, that's very different from peach

parts.note: to plug something is to advertise it

indicators.note: the speaker reports how the fruit's name sounds, not how it is spelt

parts.note: the ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo

explanation.surface: Advertising a fruit said to look nothing like a peach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peach' looks like another fruit, but here it means a beauty, so the definition is its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A peach is a lovely person; something hideous is the opposite.
